title: Case Study: The Fake Certificate Problem
description: Read the case study below regarding FutureTech University's certificate verification system and select the correct outcome.

data.problem_statement:
Case Study: The Fake Certificate Problem

📖 Case
FutureTech University issues digital certificates to students after graduation. Companies often ask students to submit these certificates while applying for jobs.

Recently, the university discovered that some students were editing their digital certificates using image-editing software. For example, a student who actually received a B grade changed the certificate to show an A grade.

To solve this problem, the university introduces a blockchain-based certificate verification system.

When a genuine certificate is issued:
• The university creates the certificate.
• A unique hash is generated from the certificate.
• The hash is recorded on a blockchain.
• The original certificate is stored securely by the university.
• The student receives a QR code on the certificate.

When an employer scans the QR code, the system calculates the hash of the certificate being presented and compares it with the hash recorded on the blockchain.

⚠️ The Situation
A student named Rahul receives a certificate showing:
• Course: BCA Cybersecurity
• Grade: B
• Certificate ID: FT2026-1045

Rahul edits his copy of the certificate and changes:
• Grade: B → A

He does not have access to the university's blockchain or its private systems. He then submits the modified certificate to a company.

The company scans the QR code and starts the verification process.

❓ QUESTION
What will most likely happen when the company verifies Rahul's modified certificate?
options: A. The certificate will be rejected because changing the certificate changes its hash, causing it to differ from the hash recorded on the blockchain.
B. The certificate will be accepted because Rahul only changed the grade and not the certificate ID.
C. The blockchain will automatically change the recorded grade from B to A.
D. The certificate will be accepted because blockchain cannot detect changes made to digital files.
acceptable_answers: The certificate will be rejected because changing the certificate changes its hash, causing it to differ from the hash recorded on the blockchain.
data.explanation: Option A is correct. Blockchain verification relies on cryptographic hash comparison. Any alteration to the certificate (such as changing Grade B to A) generates a completely different cryptographic hash. When the company scans the QR code, the calculated hash will not match the original hash stored immutably on the blockchain, causing the system to reject the fake certificate.
